overrides.reason: HF2432 creates a BCA Financial Crimes and Fraud Section focused on fraud involving state-funded or state-administered programs, requires qualifying state-agency fraud referrals, and requires annual fraud reporting. That directly implements stronger oversight and accountability for state programs to reduce fraud and waste.

HF2432 requires state agencies to refer suspected fraudulent activity at or above the statutory threshold, permits lower-dollar referrals, requires annual agency fraud reporting, and adds a BCA fraud-investigation section. That directly matches stricter state-agency fraud reporting and additional fraud-prevention tools.

SF2216 directly excludes children's off-highway vehicles, ATVs, off-highway motorcycles, snowmobiles, electric-assisted bicycles, and replacement parts from the PFAS-regulated juvenile-product definition, matching the member's exemption proposition.

SF2216 narrows existing PFAS product restrictions by adding explicit product exemptions, so it is substantively applicable to the member's opposition to rolling back Minnesota PFAS prevention measures and conflicts with that stance.

HF2438 directly increases the all-electric vehicle surcharge from $75 to $200 and allocates the revenue to transportation funds, implementing the member's proposition that EV registration charges should contribute more comparably to road funding.

HF2309 gives preference to comparable housing proposals that obtain regulatory changes or waivers producing measurable cost reductions, including increased density and zoning-code changes. That materially implements the member's proposition of easing zoning constraints to increase housing supply and affordability.

HF2432 materially implements multiple explicit elements of the member's Make Minnesota Safe package, including mandatory minimum first-degree sex-trafficking sentences, stronger mandatory/consecutive penalties for specified assaults involving jailed offenders and law enforcement, and public reporting of charging decisions.

HF2438 amends ignition-interlock eligibility and restrictions, including provisions keyed to prior impaired-driving incidents, but the exact version does not clearly establish the source proposition's combined policy of materially longer repeat-DWI interlock time plus reduced entry barriers. Same-program overlap is insufficient.
